mishnayos.summary: When a woman finds she has become tamei, from when do the things she touched become tamei? Shammai, Hillel and the Sages each give a different answer.

chunks.en: Shammai says:
For all women, their own time is enough.
chunks.explain: Only things touched from the time she found it become tamei.

chunks.en: And Hillel says:
from one check to the next check,
chunks.explain: Everything she touched since she last checked becomes tamei.

words.note: A time she checked herself and found she was still tahor.

chunks.en: even for many days.
And the Sages say:

chunks.he: לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה,
chunks.en: not like this one's words and not like that one's words,
but twenty-four hours makes it shorter

words.note: From this time yesterday until now: twenty-four hours.

chunks.en: than from check to check,
and from check to check makes it shorter
than twenty-four hours.
chunks.explain: We follow whichever time is shorter.

chunks.en: Any woman who has a set time,

words.note: A regular time when this tumah comes.

chunks.en: her own time is enough.
One who checks with cloths,

words.note: Cloths used to check whether she is tahor.

chunks.en: this counts like a check,
it makes it shorter than twenty-four hours
and than from check to check.

mishnayos.summary: How much dough must there be before we have to take challah from it? Shammai, Hillel and the Sages argue about the amount.

chunks.en: Shammai says:
from one kav, for challah.
chunks.explain: A kav is a measure of flour.

words.note: A piece of dough given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: And Hillel says:
from two kavim. And the Sages say:

chunks.he: לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה,
chunks.en: not like this one's words and not like that one's words,
but a kav and a half must have challah taken.
And when the measures were made bigger, they said:
five quarters must have challah taken.
Rabbi Yose says:
five quarters do not need it,
five and a little more must have it.

mishnayos.summary: How much drawn water ruins a mikveh? Hillel and Shammai argue, until two weavers came and told what Shemayah and Avtalyon had taught.

chunks.en: Hillel says:
a full hin of drawn water
chunks.explain: Water carried in a bucket, not water that came by itself.

words.note: A measure of liquid.

chunks.en: makes the mikveh not kosher;

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁאָדָם חַיָּב לוֹמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹ.
chunks.en: he said hin only because a person must say it in his teacher's words.
And Shammai says:
nine kavim.
And the Sages say:

chunks.he: לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה,
chunks.en: not like this one's words and not like that one's words,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁבָּאוּ שְׁנֵי גַרְדִּיִּים מִשַּׁעַר
chunks.en: but until two weavers came from the gate

chunks.he: הָאַשְׁפּוֹת שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וְהֵעִידוּ מִשּׁוּם שְׁמַעְיָה וְאַבְטַלְיוֹן,
chunks.en: of the Dung Gate in Yerushalayim and testified in the name of Shemayah and Avtalyon:

words.note: The name of one of the gates of Yerushalayim.
The teachers of Shammai and Hillel.

chunks.en: three lugin of drawn water

words.note: A small measure of liquid.

chunks.en: make the mikveh not kosher,
and the Sages accepted their words.

mishnayos.summary: Why does the Mishnah tell us what Shammai and Hillel said, if we do not follow them? To teach that a person should not hold on stubbornly to his opinion.

chunks.en: And why do we mention the words
of Shammai and Hillel for nothing?
To teach the future generations that a person
should not stand firm on his words,
since the fathers of the world did not

words.note: Great leaders, like Shammai and Hillel.

chunks.en: stand firm on their words.

mishnayos.summary: Why does the Mishnah tell us the opinion of one Sage when the halachah follows the many? So that a later beis din can rely on it.

chunks.he: וְלָמָּה מַזְכִּירִין דִּבְרֵי הַיָּחִיד בֵּין הַמְרֻבִּין,
chunks.en: And why do we mention the words of one person among the many,

chunks.he: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין הֲלָכָה אֶלָּא כְדִבְרֵי הַמְרֻבִּין.
chunks.en: since the halachah is only like the words of the many?
So that if a beis din sees

words.note: A court of Torah judges.

chunks.en: the words of the one and relies on him.
For a beis din cannot cancel
the words of another beis din unless
it is greater than it in wisdom and in number.
If it was greater than it in wisdom
but not in number,
in number but not in wisdom,
it cannot cancel its words,

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גָדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ בְחָכְמָה וּבְמִנְיָן:
chunks.en: unless it is greater than it in wisdom and in number.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehudah gives another reason for writing down the opinion of one Sage: so that if someone says "this is what I was taught," we can tell him it was only that Sage's opinion.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said:
If so, why do we mention the words
of the one among the many for nothing?

chunks.he: שֶׁאִם יֹאמַר הָאָדָם כָּךְ אֲנִי מְקֻבָּל,
chunks.en: So that if a person says, "This is what I was taught,"
we can say to him:
"You heard it as the words of So-and-so."

mishnayos.summary: How many bones of a dead person make a tent tamei? Beis Shammai, Beis Hillel and Shammai each give an amount.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
a quarter-kav of bones from the bones,
chunks.explain: This much makes things in the same tent tamei.

chunks.en: whether from two or from three people.
And Beis Hillel say:
a quarter-kav of bones from one body,
from most of the frame or most of the number of bones.
Shammai says:
even from one bone.

mishnayos.summary: Karshinim are a kind of bean usually fed to animals. If they are terumah, how careful must we be to keep them tahor?

chunks.en: Karshinim of terumah,

words.note: A kind of bean, mostly fed to animals.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
we soak them and rub them while staying tahor,
and we feed them to animals even while tamei.
Beis Hillel say:
we soak them while staying tahor,
and we rub and feed them even while tamei.
Shammai says:
they should be eaten dry.
Rabbi Akiva says:
everything done with them may be done while tamei.

mishnayos.summary: Someone changes a big coin of maaser sheni money into smaller coins. How much of it may he change into copper coins?

chunks.en: One who changes a sela of maaser sheni money,
chunks.explain: Money used to buy food to eat in Yerushalayim.

words.note: A big silver coin.
A tenth of the crops.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
for the whole sela, copper coins.
And Beis Hillel say:
for a shekel of silver and a shekel of copper coins.

words.note: Half a sela.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: אֵין מְחַלְּלִין כֶּסֶף וּפֵרוֹת עַל הַכֶּסֶף.
chunks.en: we do not switch silver and fruit onto silver.
And the Sages allow it.

mishnayos.summary: Now someone changes a sela of maaser sheni money in Yerushalayim. How much may he change into copper coins to spend there?

chunks.he: הַפּוֹרֵט סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם,
chunks.en: One who changes a sela of maaser sheni in Yerushalayim,
Beis Shammai say:
for the whole sela, copper coins.
And Beis Hillel say:
for a shekel of silver and a shekel of copper coins.
Those who argued before the Sages say:
for three dinars of silver and one dinar of copper coins.

words.note: Silver coins; four make a sela.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
for three dinars of silver, and for a quarter
of silver, a quarter in copper coins.
And Rabbi Tarfon says:
four silver aspers.

words.note: Small silver coins.

chunks.en: Shammai says:
he should leave it in the shop and eat its worth.

mishnayos.summary: A bride's chair or a seat built onto a kneading trough: can they become tamei? Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue.

chunks.en: A bride's chair whose covers were taken off,
Beis Shammai say it can become tamei,
and Beis Hillel say it stays tahor.
Shammai says:
even the frame of a chair can become tamei.
A seat that was fixed onto a kneading trough,
Beis Shammai say it can become tamei,
and Beis Hillel say it stays tahor.
Shammai says:
even one made as part of it.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Hillel changed their minds to teach like Beis Shammai. If a woman comes from far away and says her husband died, she may marry again and also collect her kesubah.

chunks.en: These are things where Beis Hillel went back
to teach like the words of Beis Shammai.
A woman who came from a faraway land

words.note: A faraway country.

chunks.en: and said, "My husband died,"
may marry again. "My husband died,"
she may do yibum. And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.explain: Marry her husband's brother.

chunks.en: We only heard this about one who came
from the harvest alone.
Beis Shammai said to them:

chunks.he: אַחַת הַבָּאָה מִן הַקָּצִיר וְאַחַת הַבָּאָה
chunks.en: It is the same if she came from the harvest, or came

chunks.he: מִן הַזֵּיתִים וְאַחַת הַבָּאָה מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: from the olives, or came from a faraway land;
they spoke of the harvest only because that is what happened.

chunks.he: חָזְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּבֵית שַׁמָּאי.
chunks.en: Beis Hillel went back to teach like Beis Shammai.
Beis Shammai say:
she may marry and take her kesubah.

words.note: The money a husband promises his wife.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
she may marry but not take her kesubah.
Beis Shammai said to them:
You allowed the strict thing, a forbidden marriage,
will you not allow the easy thing, money?
Beis Hillel said to them:
We find that the brothers do not come in
to the inheritance because of her word.
Beis Shammai said to them:
But can we not learn from her kesubah paper,
where he writes to her:
"If you marry another man,
you take what is written for you."
Beis Hillel went back to teach
like the words of Beis Shammai.

mishnayos.summary: A man who is half a slave and half free cannot marry anyone. Beis Shammai say his master must be made to free him, and Beis Hillel agreed.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין,
chunks.en: One who is half a slave and half free,
works for his master one day
and for himself one day,
these are the words of Beis Hillel.
Beis Shammai said to them:
You took care of his master,
but you did not take care of him.
To marry a maidservant,
he cannot.
A free woman,
he cannot.
Should he not marry? But the world was only created
for having children,
as it says (Yeshayahu 45):
"He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in."
Rather, to fix the world,

chunks.he: כּוֹפִין אֶת רַבּוֹ וְעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ בֶן
chunks.en: we force his master and he makes him

chunks.he: חוֹרִין וְכוֹתֵב שְׁטָר עַל חֲצִי דָמָיו.
chunks.en: free, and the slave writes a note for half his worth.

words.note: A paper saying he owes money.

chunks.he: חָזְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּבֵית שַׁמָּאי:
chunks.en: Beis Hillel went back to teach like Beis Shammai.

mishnayos.summary: A sealed clay pot in a tent with a dead body keeps what is inside it tahor. What does it protect? Beis Hillel agreed with Beis Shammai.

chunks.en: A clay pot protects everything,
chunks.explain: If it is sealed and in a tent with a dead body.

chunks.en: like the words of Beis Hillel.
And Beis Shammai say:
it protects only foods
and drinks and clay vessels.
Beis Hillel said to them:
Why?
Beis Shammai said to them:
Because it is tamei on
account of an am ha'aretz,

words.note: A person who is not careful about tumah.

chunks.en: and a tamei vessel does not block.
Beis Hillel said to them:
But you said the foods and drinks in it are tahor!
Beis Shammai said to them:
When we said the foods and drinks in it are tahor,
we made them tahor only for him.
But when you make the vessel tahor,
you make it tahor for you and for him.
Beis Hillel went back to teach
like the words of Beis Shammai.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Chanina, the assistant of the Kohanim, told what the Kohanim always did: they burned meat that was a little tamei together with meat that was more tamei, even though it made it more tamei.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina, the assistant of the Kohanim,

words.note: The helper of the Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: testified about four things.

chunks.he: מִימֵיהֶם שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים לֹא נִמְנְעוּ מִלִּשְׂרֹף
chunks.en: In all the days of the Kohanim, they never held back from burning

chunks.he: אֶת הַבָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִּוְלַד הַטֻּמְאָה עִם
chunks.en: the meat that became tamei from a lower kind of tumah together with

words.note: A lighter kind of tumah.

chunks.en: the meat that became tamei from a main kind of tumah,

words.note: A main, strong kind of tumah.

chunks.en: even though they add
tumah onto its tumah.
Rabbi Akiva added:
In all the days of the Kohanim, they never held back
from lighting the oil that became unfit through a tevul

words.note: Someone who went to the mikveh today but must wait until night to be fully tahor.

chunks.en: yom, in a lamp that became tamei from a dead body,
even though they add
tumah onto its tumah.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Chanina never saw the skin of a bechor animal taken out to be burned. Rabbi Akiva learned from this that the Kohanim may use it, but the Sages say not seeing something is no proof.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina, the assistant of the Kohanim, said:
In all my days I never saw a hide
going out to the burning place.
Rabbi Akiva said:
From his words we learned
that if someone skins a bechor and it turns out to be a treifah,

words.note: A firstborn animal, given to the Kohen.
An animal with a sickness that makes it not kosher.

chunks.en: the Kohanim may use its hide.
And the Sages say:
"We did not see" is not a proof,
but it goes out to the burning place.

mishnayos.summary: In a village near Yerushalayim, an old man wrote the loan papers himself and others signed, and the Sages allowed it. So a woman may write her own get, because the witnesses' signatures are what count. He also taught about a needle found in meat.

chunks.en: He also testified about a village
that was small, next to Yerushalayim,
and there was one old man in it who
lent money to all the people of the village, and wrote
the note in his own handwriting, and others signed,
and the case came before the Sages and they allowed it.
By your way of thinking you learn
that a woman may write her own get,

words.note: A paper that ends a marriage.

chunks.en: and a man may write his own receipt,
because a get is made firm only by its witnesses' signatures.
And about a needle found in the meat,
that the knife and the hands are tahor,
and the meat is tamei.
And if it was found in the waste inside the animal,

words.note: What is in the animal's stomach.

chunks.en: everything is tahor.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yishmael said three things in Yavneh: about a mixed-up egg on top of vegetables of terumah, about a stalk of grain left in the field, and about a small garden surrounded by vines.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael said three things
before the Sages in the vineyard in Yavneh.
chunks.explain: The Sages sat in rows, like a vineyard.

chunks.en: About a beaten egg that is placed
on top of a vegetable of terumah,
that it counts as joined to it.
And if it was shaped like a hat,
it is not joined.

chunks.he: וְעַל שִׁבֹּלֶת שֶׁבַּקָּצִיר וְרֹאשָׁהּ מַגִּיעַ לַקָּמָה,
chunks.en: And about a stalk at harvest time whose top reaches the standing grain,
if it can be cut together with the standing grain,
then it belongs to the owner,
and if not,
then it belongs to the poor.

chunks.he: וְעַל גִּנָּה קְטַנָּה שֶׁהִיא מֻקֶּפֶת עָרִיס,
chunks.en: And about a small garden that is surrounded by a row of vines,

chunks.he: אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ כִּמְלֹא בוֹצֵר וְסַלּוֹ
chunks.en: if there is room in it for a grape-picker and his basket
on this side and room for a grape-picker and his basket on that side,
it may be planted. And if not,
it may not be planted.

mishnayos.summary: Three questions were asked before Rabbi Yishmael, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Matya explained them: opening a sore on Shabbos, catching a snake on Shabbos, and special pans.

chunks.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אָמְרוּ לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
chunks.en: Three things were said before Rabbi Yishmael,

chunks.he: וְלֹא אָמַר בָּהֶם לֹא אִסּוּר וְהֶתֵּר,
chunks.en: and he said neither forbidden nor allowed about them,
and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Matya explained them.
One who opens a sore on Shabbos,
if to make an opening for it,
he is guilty; and if to let liquid out of it,
he is free. And about one who catches a snake on Shabbos,
if he is busy with it so that it should not bite him,
he is free; and if it is for medicine,
he is guilty. And about Ironian pans,

words.note: A kind of clay cooking pan.

chunks.en: that they stay tahor in a tent with a dead body
and become tamei when a zav carries them.

words.note: A man with a kind of tumah that comes from his body.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok says:
even when a zav carries them,
they are tahor, because they are not finished being made.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yishmael said three things and Rabbi Akiva did not agree. One of them: garlic and unripe grapes crushed before Shabbos, may he finish after dark?

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael said three things
and Rabbi Akiva did not agree with him.

chunks.he: הַשּׁוּם וְהַבֹּסֶר וְהַמְּלִילוֹת שֶׁרִסְּקָן מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
chunks.en: Garlic, unripe grapes, and ears of grain that he crushed while it was still day,
that Rabbi Yishmael says:
he may finish after it gets dark,
and Rabbi Akiva says:
he may not finish.

mishnayos.summary: Three things were said before Rabbi Akiva: a woman may go out on Shabbos with a golden crown, people who race pigeons cannot be witnesses, and a doubt about a weasel touching terumah loaves.

chunks.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אָמְרוּ לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
chunks.en: Three things were said before Rabbi Akiva,
two in the name of Rabbi Eliezer
and one in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua.
Two in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
a woman may go out on Shabbos with a "city of gold,"
chunks.explain: A golden crown shaped like Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: and people who race pigeons cannot be witnesses.
chunks.explain: They bet on their pigeons for money.

chunks.en: And one in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
a sheretz in a weasel's mouth, and it walks on

words.note: A small creature whose body, when dead, makes things tamei.

chunks.en: top of loaves of terumah,
maybe it touched, maybe it did not touch,
its doubt is tahor.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva said three things. The Sages agreed with him about a worker's shoe and a broken oven, but not about a chair missing two side pieces.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said three things,
about two they agreed with him and about
one they did not agree with him.
About the shoe of lime workers,
that it can become tamei from a zav stepping on it.

words.note: Tumah from a zav standing or sitting on it.

chunks.en: And about what is left of an oven: four,
when they used to say three.
And they agreed with him.
And about one they did not agree with him:
about a chair that had two of its
side pieces taken off, one next to the other,
that Rabbi Akiva says it can become tamei, and the Sages say it is tahor.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva taught that a father passes on many good things to his son, and that Hashem counts the generations until the time the redemption will come.

chunks.en: He used to say:
a father passes good things to his son:
in good looks, and in strength,
and in wealth, and in wisdom,
and in years, and in the number of generations before him,
and that is the end time,
as it says (Yeshayahu 41): "He calls the generations from the beginning."
Even though it says (Bereishis 15):

chunks.he: וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אֹתָם אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה,
chunks.en: "And they will make them work and hurt them for four hundred years,"

words.en: and they will make them work

chunks.en: and it says (there):
"And the fourth generation will come back here."

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva also taught five judgments that lasted, or will last, twelve months: the Flood, Iyov, the Egyptians, Gog and Magog, and the wicked in Gehinnom.

chunks.en: He also used to say:

chunks.he: חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים שֶׁל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
chunks.en: five things last twelve months.
The judgment of the generation of the Flood,
twelve months.
The judgment of Iyov,
twelve months.
The judgment of the Egyptians,
twelve months.
The judgment of Gog and Magog in the time to come,
twelve months.
The judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom,
twelve months,
as it says (Yeshayahu 66):
"And it will be, from month to month."
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
from Pesach until Shavuos,
as it says, "and from Shabbos to Shabbos."

mishnayos.summary: Things that make tamei, when split into two halves, can they still join together to make a person tamei? Rabbi Dosa says no, and the Sages say yes, unless the two halves make him tamei in two different ways.

chunks.en: All things that make tamei in a tent which were split,
and he brought them into the house,
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says it is tahor,
and the Sages say it is tamei.
How is this? One who touches two halves of an olive's size

words.note: The size of half an olive.

chunks.en: of a neveilah, or carries them,

words.note: An animal that died without shechitah.

chunks.he: וּבַמֵּת, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכַחֲצִי זַיִת וּמַאֲהִיל עַל
chunks.en: and with a dead person: one who touches half an olive's size and is over
half an olive's size, or touches half
an olive's size and half an olive's size is over him,
or is over two halves of an olive's size,
is over half an olive's size
and half an olive's size is over him,
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas
says tahor and the Sages say tamei.

chunks.he: אֲבָל הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכַחֲצִי זַיִת וְדָבָר אַחֵר
chunks.en: But one who touches half an olive's size, and something else
is over him and over half an olive's size,

chunks.he: אוֹ מַאֲהִיל עַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וְדָבָר
chunks.en: or is over half an olive's size, and something

chunks.he: אַחֵר מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו וְעַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת,
chunks.en: else is over him and over half an olive's size,
is tahor. Rabbi Meir said:
even here Rabbi Dosa
says tahor and the Sages say tamei.
Everything is tamei,
except touching together with carrying,
and carrying together with a tent.
This is the rule:
whatever is from one name
chunks.explain: The same kind of tumah, like two touchings.

chunks.en: is tamei. From two names, it is tahor.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Dosa and the Sages argue about three things: whether pieces of food add up, whether maaser sheni can be switched onto a blank coin, and dipping hands for the parah adumah.

chunks.en: Food in separate pieces
does not add up,
the words of Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas.
And the Sages say:

chunks.he: מִצְטָרֵף. מְחַלְּלִין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי עַל אֲסִימוֹן,
chunks.en: it adds up. We may redeem maaser sheni onto a blank coin,

words.note: A metal coin with no picture stamped on it yet.

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
we may not redeem.
We may dip just the hands for the chatas water,
chunks.explain: The water mixed with ashes of the parah adumah.

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
if his hands became tamei,
his whole body became tamei.

mishnayos.summary: May a non-Kohen eat the inside of a terumah melon or the thrown-away leaves of terumah vegetables? And how much wool from five sheep must be given to the Kohen?

chunks.he: מְעֵי אֲבַטִּיחַ וּקְנִיבַת יָרָק שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
chunks.en: The inside of a melon and the trimmed leaves of a vegetable of terumah,
Rabbi Dosa allows them to non-Kohanim,
and the Sages forbid.

chunks.he: חָמֵשׁ רְחֵלוֹת גְּזוּזוֹת מָנֶה מָנֶה וּפְרַס,
chunks.en: Five sheep whose wool came to a maneh and a half each,

words.note: A weight.

chunks.en: must give the first of the shearing,

words.note: Some wool that is given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
five sheep, any amount at all.

mishnayos.summary: Which mats and woven things can become tamei? Rabbi Dosa and the Sages argue.

chunks.en: All mats can become tamei from a dead body,
the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
from treading. All woven bands are tahor,

words.note: Tumah from a zav standing or sitting on it.

chunks.en: except those of a galgilon,

words.note: A kind of belt or band.

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
all of them can become tamei,
except those of wool workers.

mishnayos.summary: A sling for throwing stones: when can it become tamei, and when is it tahor?

chunks.en: A sling whose holder is woven,
can become tamei. And one of leather,
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas
says tahor and the Sages say tamei.
If its finger loop was torn off,
it is tahor. If its holding-strap was torn off, it is tamei.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who was taken captive: may she still eat terumah? It depends on whether we only know about it from her own words.

chunks.en: A woman who was taken captive may eat terumah,
the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
there is a captive woman who eats and there is
a captive woman who does not eat.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁאָמְרָה נִשְׁבֵּיתִי וּטְהוֹרָה אָנִי,
chunks.en: How? A woman who said, "I was captured, and I am tahor,"

chunks.he: אוֹכֶלֶת, שֶׁהַפֶּה שֶׁאָסַר הוּא הַפֶּה שֶׁהִתִּיר.
chunks.en: eats, because the mouth that forbade is the mouth that allowed.
chunks.explain: We only know she was captured from her own words.

chunks.en: And if there are witnesses that she was captured,
and she says, "I am tahor,"
she does not eat.

mishnayos.summary: In four cases of doubt about whether something touched tumah, Rabbi Yehoshua says it is tamei and the Sages say it is tahor.

chunks.en: Four doubts that Rabbi Yehoshua says are tamei,
and the Sages say are tahor.
How? The tamei one stands and the tahor one passes by,
the tahor one stands and the tamei one passes by,

chunks.he: טֻמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְטָהֳרָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: tumah in a private place and taharah in a public place,

chunks.he: טָהֳרָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְטֻמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: taharah in a private place and tumah in a public place,
maybe he touched, maybe he did not touch,
maybe he was over it, maybe he was not over it,
maybe he moved it, maybe he did not move it,
Rabbi Yehoshua says tamei,
and the Sages say tahor.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Tzadok says three metal or wooden things can become tamei, and the Sages say they cannot.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tzadok says three things are tamei,
and the Sages say tahor:
the nail of a money changer,
and a chest of grist-makers,

words.note: People who grind beans and grain.

chunks.en: and the nail of a sundial stone,

words.note: A sundial that tells the time.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tzadok says tamei and the Sages say tahor.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel says four metal things can become tamei and the Sages say they cannot. The Sages agree about a tablet split into a big piece and a small piece.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says four things are tamei,
and the Sages say tahor:
a metal cover of a basket
of homeowners,
and the hook for scrapers,

words.note: Metal tools used to scrape the skin in the bathhouse.

chunks.en: and unfinished metal vessels,
and a tablet that was split in two.
And the Sages agree with Rabban Gamliel
about a tablet that was split in two,
one big and one small,
the big one is tamei and the small one is tahor.

mishnayos.summary: In three things about Yom Tov, Rabban Gamliel was strict like Beis Shammai. The Sages said his family could be strict on themselves but allowed it for all Yisrael.

chunks.en: In three things Rabban Gamliel
is strict like the words of Beis Shammai.
We do not wrap up hot food
from Yom Tov for Shabbos,

chunks.he: וְאֵין זוֹקְפִין אֶת הַמְּנוֹרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: and we do not put together the menorah on Yom Tov,

chunks.he: וְאֵין אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין.
chunks.en: and we do not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.he: מִימֵיהֶן שֶׁל בֵּית אַבָּא לֹא הָיוּ
chunks.en: In all the days of my father's house they did not
bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
They said to him:

chunks.he: מַה נַּעֲשֶׂה לְבֵית אָבִיךָ שֶׁהָיוּ מַחְמִירִין
chunks.en: What can we do about your father's house, who were strict

chunks.he: עַל עַצְמָן וּמְקִלִּין עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת
chunks.en: on themselves and easy on Yisrael, letting them
bake thick loaves and white bread.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel also allowed three things on Yom Tov: sweeping between the beds, putting spices on coals, and making a roasted goat on Pesach night. The Sages forbid them.

chunks.he: אַף הוּא אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים לְהָקֵל.
chunks.en: He also said three things to be easy.
We may sweep between the beds,
and put the spices on the coals on Yom Tov,

words.note: Sweet-smelling spices put on hot coals.

chunks.en: and make a whole roasted goat on Pesach night.
And the Sages forbid.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah allowed three things that the Sages forbid: his cow going out on Shabbos with a strap, combing an animal on Yom Tov, and grinding pepper in a pepper mill.

chunks.en: Three things that Rabbi Elazar
ben Azaryah allows,
and the Sages forbid.
His cow went out with a strap between her horns,
and we may comb an animal on Yom Tov,
and we may grind the peppers in their own mill.
Rabbi Yehudah says:

chunks.he: אֵין מְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: we may not comb an animal on Yom Tov,
because it makes a wound,
but we may scrape it.
And the Sages say:
we may not comb, and we may not even scrape.

mishnayos.summary: Here begin cases where Beis Shammai are easier and Beis Hillel are stricter. First: an egg laid on Yom Tov, and how much se'or and chametz is forbidden on Pesach.

chunks.en: These are things that are among the easy rulings of Beis
Shammai and the strict rulings of Beis Hillel.

words.en: and from the strict rulings of

chunks.en: An egg that was laid on Yom Tov,
Beis Shammai say:
it may be eaten. And Beis Hillel say:
it may not be eaten.
Beis Shammai say:
se'or is an olive's size and chametz is a date's size.
chunks.explain: Se'or is dough so sour it makes other dough rise.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
both this and that are an olive's size.

mishnayos.summary: An animal born on Yom Tov may be eaten, but a chick that hatched may not. If someone does shechitah on a wild animal or a bird on Yom Tov, how may he cover the blood?

chunks.en: An animal that was born on Yom Tov,
everyone agrees that it is allowed.
And a chick that came out of the egg,
everyone agrees that it is forbidden.
One who does shechitah on a wild animal or a bird on Yom Tov,
Beis Shammai say:
he may dig with a pick and cover the blood.
chunks.explain: The Torah says to cover their blood with earth.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
he should not do shechitah unless
he had earth ready.
And they agree that if he already did shechitah,
he may dig with a pick and cover.
Because ashes from a stove count as ready.

mishnayos.summary: Is something made hefker only for the poor really hefker? And when is a big sheaf that was forgotten in the field left for the poor?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
ownerless for the poor
is ownerless. And Beis Hillel say:
it is not ownerless,
until it is made ownerless for the rich too, like in shemittah.

words.note: The seventh year, when all fields are open to everyone.

chunks.he: כָּל עָמְרֵי הַשָּׂדֶה שֶׁל קַב קַב,
chunks.en: All the sheaves in the field were a kav each,
and one was four kavim,
and he forgot it, Beis Shammai say:
it is not shich'chah.

words.note: A forgotten sheaf, which must be left for the poor.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say: it is shich'chah.

mishnayos.summary: A sheaf left near a wall, a stack, cattle or tools, and then forgotten: is it left for the poor?

chunks.en: A sheaf that is near the wall
or the stack or the cattle or the tools,
and he forgot it, Beis Shammai say:
it is not shich'chah.
And Beis Hillel say: it is shich'chah.

mishnayos.summary: The grapes of a vineyard in its fourth year must be eaten in Yerushalayim. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about which rules of maaser sheni and of gifts to the poor apply to it.

chunks.en: A vineyard in its fourth year,
Beis Shammai say:

chunks.he: אֵין לוֹ חֹמֶשׁ וְאֵין לוֹ בִעוּר.
chunks.en: it has no added fifth and it has no removal.
chunks.explain: Rules that apply to maaser sheni.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:

chunks.he: יֶשׁ לוֹ חֹמֶשׁ וְיֶשׁ לוֹ בִעוּר.
chunks.en: it has an added fifth and it has removal.
Beis Shammai say:

chunks.he: יֶשׁ לוֹ פֶרֶט וְיֶשׁ לוֹ עוֹלְלוֹת,
chunks.en: it has fallen grapes and small bunches for the poor,
and the poor redeem them for themselves.
And Beis Hillel say:
all of it goes to the winepress.

mishnayos.summary: A barrel of olives, and a person who rubbed himself with oil and then went to the mikveh: how much oil left on him matters?

chunks.en: A barrel of pressed olives,
Beis Shammai say:
he does not need to make a hole in it.
And Beis Hillel say:
he needs to make a hole.
And they agree that if he made a hole and the sediment plugged it,

words.en: he made a hole in it

chunks.en: it is tahor.
One who rubbed himself with tahor oil and became tamei,
went down and dipped in the mikveh,
Beis Shammai say:
even though he is dripping,
he is tahor. And Beis Hillel say:
only if there is enough to rub a small limb.
And if it was tamei oil from the start,
Beis Shammai say:
enough to rub a small limb.
And Beis Hillel say:
wet liquid.

chunks.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם בֵּית הִלֵּל,
chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says in the name of Beis Hillel:
wet enough to make something else wet.

mishnayos.summary: How much money is needed for kiddushin? And Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about some rules of a get.

chunks.en: A woman becomes engaged with a dinar or something worth a dinar,
like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
with a perutah or something worth a perutah.

words.note: The smallest coin.

chunks.en: And how much is a perutah?
One eighth of an Italian issar.

words.note: A small coin.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:

chunks.he: פּוֹטֵר הוּא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ בְגֵט יָשָׁן,
chunks.en: a man may send away his wife with an old get,
and Beis Hillel forbid.
What is an old get?

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁנִּתְיַחֵד עִמָּהּ אַחַר שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ לָהּ.
chunks.en: Any get where he stayed alone with her after he wrote it for her.

chunks.he: הַמְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְלָנָה עִמּוֹ בְפֻנְדְּקִי,
chunks.en: One who sent away his wife, and she stayed the night with him at an inn,
Beis Shammai say:
she does not need a second get from him.
And Beis Hillel say:
she needs a second get from him.
When? When she was divorced after the wedding.
But if she was divorced from being only engaged,
she does not need a second get from him,
because he is not so close with her.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argued about some marriages, yet they still married into each other's families and trusted each other about taharah.

chunks.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מַתִּירִין אֶת הַצָּרוֹת לָאַחִים,
chunks.en: Beis Shammai allow the co-wives to the brothers,
chunks.explain: When a man dies with no children, his brother may marry his wife.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel forbid.

chunks.he: חָלְצוּ, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין מִן הַכְּהֻנָּה,
chunks.en: If they did chalitzah, Beis Shammai make them unfit to marry a Kohen,

words.note: The ceremony instead of the brother marrying her.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel make them fit.
If they married the brother, Beis Shammai make them fit,
and Beis Hillel make them unfit.
And even though these
make unfit and these make fit,
Beis Shammai did not hold back
from marrying women from Beis Hillel,
and Beis Hillel did not hold back from marrying
women from Beis Shammai.
And all the cases of taharah and tumah where
these said tahor and these said tamei,
they did not hold back from preparing tahor food
with one another.

mishnayos.summary: Three brothers, two married to two sisters: if both married brothers die, what happens to the unmarried brother and the widows? Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
two of them married to two
sisters, and one not married,
one of the sisters' husbands died,
and the unmarried brother made a ma'amar with her,
chunks.explain: He said words to begin marrying her.

chunks.en: and after that his second brother died,
Beis Shammai say:
his wife stays with him,
and the other one goes free, because she is his wife's sister.
And Beis Hillel say:
he sends away his wife with a get and chalitzah,
and his brother's wife with chalitzah.
This is what they meant when they said:
"Woe to him about his wife and woe
to him about his brother's wife!"

mishnayos.summary: More cases where Beis Shammai are easier: a vow a man makes about his wife, a korban a woman brings, tzitzis on a linen sheet, and a Shabbos basket.

chunks.en: One who makes a vow to keep apart from his wife,
Beis Shammai say:
two weeks.
And Beis Hillel say:
one week.
A woman who lost a baby on the night of the eighty-first day,

words.en: a woman who lost a baby

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say she does not need a korban,
and Beis Hillel say she must bring one.
A linen sheet with tzitzis,
Beis Shammai say it is free,
and Beis Hillel say it must have them.
A Shabbos basket of fruit,
Beis Shammai say it is free from maaser,
and Beis Hillel say it must be given.

mishnayos.summary: A nazir who finished his nezirus outside Eretz Yisrael and then came there, and two groups of witnesses who say different numbers of nezirus: what is the halachah?

chunks.en: One who vowed a long nezirus and finished

words.note: A promise not to drink wine or cut hair for a time.

chunks.en: his nezirus and after that came to the Land,

words.note: Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
he is a nazir for thirty days.
And Beis Hillel say:
he is a nazir from the beginning.
One who had two groups
of witnesses testifying about him,
these testify that he vowed two
and these testify that he vowed five,
Beis Shammai say:
the testimony is split and there is no nezirus here.
And Beis Hillel say:
two is included in five,
so he is a nazir for two.

mishnayos.summary: A person lying under a crack between two rooms where there is tumah: does his body bring the tumah across?

chunks.en: A person who is lying under the crack,
Beis Shammai say:
he does not bring the tumah.
And Beis Hillel say:
a person is hollow,
and the upper side brings the tumah.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehudah lists six cases where Beis Shammai are easier and Beis Hillel are stricter, about blood of a neveilah, eggs, some kinds of tumah, shemittah fruit and a leather bottle.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
six things are among the easy rulings of Beis
Shammai and the strict rulings of Beis Hillel.

words.en: and from the strict rulings of

chunks.en: The blood of neveilos,

words.note: Animals that died without shechitah.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is tahor,
and Beis Hillel say it is tamei.
An egg found inside a neveilah,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהּ נִמְכֶּרֶת בַּשּׁוּק,
chunks.en: if eggs like it are sold in the market,
it is allowed. And if not,
it is forbidden, like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel forbid it.
And they agree that an egg of a treifah is forbidden,
because it grew while forbidden.

chunks.he: דַּם נָכְרִית וְדַם טָהֳרָה שֶׁל מְצֹרַעַת,
chunks.en: A kind of tumah of a non-Jewish woman, and of a woman who is a metzora in her tahor days,

words.en: and a kind of tumah of

words.note: A person with tzaraas.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is tahor.
And Beis Hillel say:
it is like her spit and her other liquids.
chunks.explain: It makes tamei only while it is wet.

chunks.he: אוֹכְלִין פֵּרוֹת שְׁבִיעִית בְּטוֹבָה וְשֶׁלֹּא בְטוֹבָה,
chunks.en: We may eat shemittah fruit with or without thanks to the owner,
like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
we eat only with thanks to the owner.
A leather bottle: Beis Shammai say:
only when it stands tied up.
And Beis Hillel say:
even when it is not tied up.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yose lists six more cases where Beis Shammai are easier: chicken and cheese on the table, terumah from olives and grapes, planting in a vineyard, dough, a mikveh, and a ger on erev Pesach.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yose says:
six things are among the easy rulings of Beis
Shammai and the strict rulings of Beis Hillel.

words.en: and from the strict rulings of

chunks.en: Chicken may be put together with cheese
on the table but it is not eaten together,
like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
it is not put up and it is not eaten.
We may take terumah from olives for oil,
and from grapes for wine,
like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
we may not take terumah this way.
One who plants in the four amos of the vineyard,
Beis Shammai say:
he made one row forbidden,
chunks.explain: Kilayim: planting seeds near grapevines makes them forbidden.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say:
he made two rows forbidden.
A soft dough: Beis Shammai say it is free from challah,
and Beis Hillel say it must have challah taken.
We may dip in a flowing stream of rainwater,
like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
we may not dip there.
A ger who became Jewish on erev Pesach,
Beis Shammai say:
he dips in the mikveh and eats his Pesach offering in the evening.
And Beis Hillel say:
one who just had his bris
is like one who leaves a grave.
chunks.explain: He must wait seven days to become tahor.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yishmael lists three cases where Beis Shammai are easier: Koheles, the water of the parah adumah, and a spice called ketzach.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says:
three things are among the easy rulings of Beis
Shammai and the strict rulings of Beis Hillel.

words.en: and from the strict rulings of

chunks.en: Koheles does not make the hands tamei,
chunks.explain: Holy books make hands tamei; so is Koheles a holy book?

chunks.en: like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
it makes the hands tamei.
Chatas water that was already used for its mitzvah,
Beis Shammai say it is tahor,
and Beis Hillel say it is tamei.

chunks.he: הַקֶּצַח, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְטַהֲרִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַמְּאִין.
chunks.en: Ketzach: Beis Shammai say it is tahor and Beis Hillel say it is tamei.

words.note: A kind of black seed used as a spice.

chunks.en: And the same for maaser.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer lists two cases where Beis Shammai are easier, about a kind of tumah of a woman after she has a baby.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:
two things are among the easy rulings of Beis
Shammai and the strict rulings of Beis Hillel.

words.en: and from the strict rulings of

chunks.en: The tumah of a woman after birth who did not yet go to the mikveh,
Beis Shammai say:
it is like her spit and her other liquids.
And Beis Hillel say:
it makes tamei whether wet or dry.
And they agree that a woman after birth who has zivah, it

words.en: about a woman who gave birth

words.note: A kind of tumah that comes from the body.

chunks.en: makes tamei whether wet or dry.

mishnayos.summary: Four brothers, two married to two sisters. If those two die, the other brothers do chalitzah and may not marry them.

chunks.en: Four brothers,
two of them married to two sisters,
the ones married to the sisters died,
these women do chalitzah and do not marry the brothers.
And if they went ahead and married them,

chunks.he: יוֹצִיאוּ. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי,
chunks.en: they must send them away. Rabbi Eliezer says in the name of Beis Shammai:
they may keep them. And Beis Hillel say: they must send them away.

mishnayos.summary: Akavya ben Mahalalel would not take back four rulings, even to become the head of the beis din. The Mishnah tells what happened, and Rabbi Yehudah says Akavya was never put in cherem.

chunks.he: עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל הֵעִיד אַרְבָּעָה דְבָרִים.
chunks.en: Akavya ben Mahalalel testified about four things.
They said to him:

chunks.he: עֲקַבְיָא, חֲזֹר בְּךָ בְאַרְבָּעָה דְבָרִים שֶׁהָיִיתָ אוֹמֵר
chunks.en: Akavya, take back the four things that you used to say,
and we will make you the head of the beis din of Yisrael.
He said to them:

chunks.he: מוּטָב לִי לְהִקָּרֵא שׁוֹטֶה כָּל יָמַי,
chunks.en: It is better for me to be called a fool all my days,
and not to be for one moment
wicked before Hashem,

words.note: Literally "the Place," a name for Hashem.

chunks.en: so that people should not say:
"He took it back for the sake of power."
He used to say that a "left" hair is tamei
of a spot of tzaraas, and a greenish kind of tumah.

words.note: A hair in a spot of tzaraas.
A kind of tumah of a woman.

chunks.en: And the Sages say they are tahor.
He used to allow the hair of a bechor
with a blemish that fell off and he put it in a window
and after that did shechitah on it,
and the Sages forbid.
He used to say:
we do not give the sotah water to drink, not to a woman who became a gerus
chunks.explain: A woman whose husband suspects her drinks special water.

words.en: the woman who became a ger

chunks.en: and not to a freed maidservant.
And the Sages say:
we do give them to drink. They said to him:
It happened with Karkemis,
a freed maidservant who was in Yerushalayim,
and Shemayah and Avtalyon gave her to drink.
He said to them:
They only gave her something that looked like it.
And they put him in cherem, and he died in his cherem,

words.en: and they put him in cherem
words.note: Kept away from the people as a punishment.

chunks.en: and the beis din put a stone on his coffin.
Rabbi Yehudah said:
Heaven forbid that Akavya was put in cherem,
because the Azarah was never locked on any

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: person in Yisrael as great in wisdom and fear of sin
as Akavya ben Mahalalel.
And whom did they put in cherem?
Eliezer ben Chanoch,
who doubted the washing of hands.
And when he died, the beis din sent and put
a stone on his coffin.
This teaches that anyone who is put in cherem and dies in his cherem,
we put a stone on his coffin.

mishnayos.summary: Before he died, Akavya told his son to follow the many Sages and not his own four rulings. He also taught his son that his own good deeds would bring him close to the Sages.

chunks.en: At the time of his death he said to his son:

chunks.he: בְּנִי, חֲזֹר בְּךָ בְאַרְבָּעָה דְבָרִים שֶׁהָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר.
chunks.en: My son, take back the four things that I used to say.
He said to him:
And why did you not take them back?
He said to him:
I heard it from the mouth of the many,
and they heard it from the mouth of the many.
I stood firm on what I heard,
and they stood firm on what they heard.
But you heard it from the mouth of one person,
and from the mouth of the many.
It is better to leave the words of the one,
and to hold on to the words of the many.
He said to him:
Father, speak well of me to your friends.
He said to him:
I will not ask them.
He said to him:
Maybe you found something wrong in me?
He said to him:
No. Your deeds will bring you close and your deeds will push you away.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava testified about five things he knew: about young girls, about one witness, about a rooster, about wine for the mizbe'ach, and about the morning korban tamid.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava
testified about five things.
That young girls may refuse their marriage,
chunks.explain: A young orphan girl married off by her family may say no when she grows up.

chunks.en: and that we let a woman marry again on
the word of one witness,
and that a rooster was stoned in Yerushalayim because
it killed a person,
and about wine forty days old
that was poured as a nesech on the mizbe'ach,
and about the morning tamid korban

words.note: The korban brought every morning and afternoon.

chunks.en: that was brought at four hours into the day.

mishnayos.summary: Two Sages testified that a limb from a dead person makes things tamei. Rabbi Eliezer said the rule was taught only about a limb from a living person, and explains why that tumah can be stronger.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Nechunya testified,
ben Elinasan, a man from Kfar HaBavli,

chunks.he: עַל אֵבֶר מִן הַמֵּת שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא,
chunks.en: about a limb from a dead person, that it is tamei,
because Rabbi Eliezer says:
they only said it about
a limb from a living person.
They said to him:
But is it not a kal vachomer?
chunks.explain: An "all the more so" proof.

chunks.en: If from a living person, who is tahor,
a limb that comes off from him is tamei,
then a dead person, who is tamei,
is it not right that a limb
that comes off from him is tamei?
He said to them:
They only said it about
a limb from a living person.
Another thing:
the tumah of the living is greater than the tumah of the dead,
because a living person makes a bed and a seat under him tamei,
chunks.explain: This is a zav, who has a kind of tumah from his body.

chunks.en: to make a person tamei and to make clothes tamei,

chunks.he: וְעַל גַּבָּיו מַדָּף לְטַמֵּא אֳכָלִים וּמַשְׁקִין,
chunks.en: and what is above him a madaf, to make foods and drinks tamei,

words.note: A lighter tumah of things above a zav.

chunks.en: which a dead person does not make tamei.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Nechunya and Rabbi Yehoshua argue about flesh or a small bone that comes off a limb taken from a living person, and each one explains his reasons.

chunks.he: כַּזַּיִת בָּשָׂר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מֵאֵבָר מִן הַחַי,
chunks.en: An olive's size of flesh that comes off a limb from a living person,
Rabbi Eliezer says it is tamei,
and Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Nechunya say it is tahor.

chunks.he: עֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מֵאֵבָר מִן הַחַי,
chunks.en: A bone the size of a barley grain that comes off a limb from a living person,
Rabbi Nechunya says it is tamei,
and Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua say it is tahor.
They said to Rabbi Eliezer:
What did you see to say an olive's size of flesh is tamei
that comes off a limb from a living person?
He said to them:

chunks.he: מָצִינוּ אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי כְּמֵת שָׁלֵם.
chunks.en: We find a limb from a living person is like a whole dead body.
Just like a dead body,
an olive's size of flesh that comes off it is tamei,
so too a limb from a living person,

chunks.he: כַּזַּיִת בָּשָׂר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ יִהְיֶה טָמֵא.
chunks.en: an olive's size of flesh that comes off it should be tamei.
They said to him:
No! If you said an olive's size of flesh is tamei
that comes off a dead body,

chunks.he: שֶׁכֵּן טִמֵּאתָ עֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ,
chunks.en: that is because you also said a bone the size of a barley grain from it is tamei;
will you say an olive's size of flesh is tamei that comes off
a limb from a living person,

chunks.he: שֶׁכֵּן טִהַרְתָּ עֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה הַפּוֹרֵשׁ הֵימֶנּוּ.
chunks.en: when you said a bone the size of a barley grain from it is tahor?
They said to Rabbi Nechunya:
What did you see to say a bone the size of a barley grain is tamei
that comes off a limb from a living person?
He said to them:

chunks.he: מָצִינוּ אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי כְּמֵת שָׁלֵם.
chunks.en: We find a limb from a living person is like a whole dead body.
Just like a dead body,
a bone the size of a barley grain that comes off it is tamei,
so too a limb from a living person,

chunks.he: עֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ יִהְיֶה טָמֵא.
chunks.en: a bone the size of a barley grain that comes off it should be tamei.
They said to him:
No! If you said a bone the size of a barley grain is tamei
that comes off a dead body,

chunks.he: שֶׁכֵּן טִמֵּאתָ כַזַּיִת בָּשָׂר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ,
chunks.en: that is because you also said an olive's size of flesh from it is tamei;
will you say a bone the size of a barley grain is tamei that comes off
a limb from a living person,

chunks.he: שֶׁכֵּן טִהַרְתָּ כַזַּיִת בָּשָׂר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ.
chunks.en: when you said an olive's size of flesh from it is tahor?
They said to Rabbi Eliezer:
What did you see to split your rulings?

chunks.he: אוֹ טַמֵּא בִשְׁנֵיהֶם אוֹ טַהֵר בִּשְׁנֵיהֶם.
chunks.en: Either say tamei for both or say tahor for both.
He said to them:
the tumah of flesh is greater than the tumah of bones,
because flesh counts with neveilos and with sheratzim,
which is not so with bones.
Another thing:
a limb that has the right amount of flesh on it,
makes tamei by touching, by carrying and by a tent.
If flesh is missing,
it is tamei. If bone is missing,
it is tahor. They said to Rabbi Nechunya:
What did you see to split your rulings?

chunks.he: אוֹ טַמֵּא בִשְׁנֵיהֶם אוֹ טַהֵר בִּשְׁנֵיהֶם.
chunks.en: Either say tamei for both or say tahor for both.
He said to them:
the tumah of bones is greater than the tumah of flesh,
because flesh that comes off a living person is tahor,
but a limb that comes off him,
and it is whole as it was made,
is tamei. Another thing:

chunks.he: כַּזַּיִת בָּשָׂר מְטַמֵּא בְמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא וּבְאֹהֶל,
chunks.en: an olive's size of flesh makes tamei by touching, by carrying and by a tent,

chunks.he: וְרֹב עֲצָמוֹת מְטַמְּאִים בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא וּבְאֹהֶל.
chunks.en: and most of the bones make tamei by touching, by carrying and by a tent.
If the flesh is missing,
it is tahor. If most of the bones are missing,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁטָּהוֹר מִלְּטַמֵּא בְאֹהֶל,
chunks.en: even though they are tahor from making tamei by a tent,
they make tamei by touching and by carrying.
Another thing:
all the flesh of a dead body,
that is less than an olive's size,

chunks.he: טָהוֹר. רֹב בִּנְיָנוֹ וְרֹב מִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל מֵת,
chunks.en: is tahor. Most of the frame or most of the number of bones of a dead body,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם רֹבַע,
chunks.en: even though they are not a quarter-kav,
are tamei. They said to Rabbi Yehoshua:
What did you see to say tahor for both?
He said to them:
No! If you said so about a dead body,
which has the rules of "most," "a quarter" and "grave dust,"
will you say so about a living person, who does not have
"most," "a quarter" and "grave dust"?

mishnayos.summary: A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb for the Kohen. If that lamb died before the Kohen got it, the owner does not have to give another one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Tzadok testified
about the redemption lamb of a firstborn donkey that died,
that the Kohen gets nothing from it,
because Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.he: חַיָּבִין בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן כְּחָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים שֶׁל בֵּן.
chunks.en: they must make up for it, like the five sela'im of a son.
chunks.explain: The money for pidyon haben, redeeming a firstborn boy.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
they do not have to make up for it, but
it is like the redemption of maaser sheni.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Tzadok testified that the juice of non-kosher locusts pickled with kosher locusts does not make the juice forbidden.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tzadok testified about
the juice of non-kosher locusts,
that it is tahor.
Because the first Mishnah taught:

chunks.he: חֲגָבִים טְמֵאִים שֶׁנִּכְבְּשׁוּ עִם חֲגָבִים טְהוֹרִים,
chunks.en: non-kosher locusts that were pickled with kosher locusts
do not make their juice unfit.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Tzadok testified that if flowing water is mixed with more dripping water, the mikveh is still kosher. This really happened, and the Sages said it was kosher.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tzadok testified about
flowing water that became more than dripping water,
that it is kosher.
It happened in Birat HaPilya,
and the case came before the Sages and they said it was kosher.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Tzadok testified that flowing water poured through a nut leaf is kosher. This really happened, and the great beis din said it was kosher.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tzadok testified about
flowing water that was poured through a nut leaf,
that it is kosher.
It happened in Ahaliya,

chunks.he: וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי לִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית, וְהִכְשִׁירוּהוּ:
chunks.en: and the case came before the Lishkas HaGazis, and they said it was kosher.

words.note: Where the Sanhedrin sat in the Beis HaMikdash.

mishnayos.summary: A jug for the parah adumah ashes that was placed on a sheretz is tamei. And Rabbi Papyas taught how a nazir who took two nezirus counts his days.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Yakim testified,
a man from Hadar, about a jug of
chatas ashes that he put on top of a sheretz,
that it is tamei.
Because Rabbi Eliezer says it is tahor.
Rabbi Papyas testified about
one who vowed two nezirus,

chunks.he: שֶׁאִם גִּלַּח אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים,
chunks.en: that if he shaved for the first one on day thirty,
he shaves for the second on day sixty.

chunks.he: וְאִם גִלַּח יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים חָסֵר אֶחָד,
chunks.en: And if he shaved on day sixty minus one,

chunks.he: יָצָא, שֶׁיּוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים עוֹלֶה לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן:
chunks.en: he is done, because day thirty counts for him in the number.

mishnayos.summary: The baby of an animal brought as a shelamim may also be brought as a shelamim. Rabbi Papyas tells about a cow his family had.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Papyas testified
about the baby of a shelamim animal,

words.note: A korban that the owner shares in eating.

chunks.en: that it is brought as a shelamim.
Because Rabbi Eliezer says that the baby
of a shelamim is not brought as a shelamim.
And the Sages say:
it is brought. Rabbi Papyas said:
I testify that we had
a cow that was a shelamim korban,

chunks.he: וַאֲכַלְנוּהָ בַפֶּסַח וְאָכַלְנוּ וְלָדָהּ שְׁלָמִים בֶּחָג:
chunks.en: and we ate it on Pesach, and we ate its baby as a shelamim on Sukkos.

mishnayos.summary: More testimonies: about bakers' boards, an oven cut into rings, adding a month in Adar, and making a leap year on a condition, as happened with Rabban Gamliel.

chunks.he: הֵם הֵעִידוּ עַל אֲרוּכוֹת שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִים,
chunks.en: They testified about the boards of bakers,
that they can become tamei.
Because Rabbi Eliezer says they are tahor.

chunks.he: הֵם הֵעִידוּ עַל תַּנּוּר שֶׁחִתְּכוֹ חֻלְיוֹת
chunks.en: They testified about an oven that was cut into rings,
and he put sand between one ring and the next,
that it can become tamei.
Because Rabbi Eliezer says it is tahor.
They testified that we may add a month to

words.en: that we add a month to

chunks.en: the year during all of Adar.
Because people used to say only until Purim.
They testified that we may add a month to

words.en: that we add a month to

chunks.en: the year on a condition.
And it happened that Rabban Gamliel went to get
permission from a governor in Syria, and he was late coming back,
and they added a month to the year on

words.en: and they added a month to

chunks.en: the condition that Rabban Gamliel would want it,
and when he came he said, "I want it,"
and the year was found to have the extra month.

mishnayos.summary: Menachem ben Signai testified about the rim added to a big pot: for olive boilers it can become tamei, and for dyers it is tahor.

chunks.he: הֵעִיד מְנַחֵם בֶּן סִגְנַאי עַל מוּסַף
chunks.en: Menachem ben Signai testified about the added rim

chunks.he: הַיּוֹרָה שֶׁל שׁוֹלְקֵי זֵיתִים שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא,
chunks.en: of the pot of olive boilers, that it can become tamei,
and of dyers, that it is tahor.
Because people used to say the opposite.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Nechunya ben Gudgeda testified about four things: a deaf girl's marriage, a young girl married to a Kohen, a stolen beam built into a building, and a stolen chatas korban.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nechunya ben Gudgeda testified
about a deaf girl whose father married her off,
that she can leave the marriage with a get.

chunks.he: וְעַל קְטַנָּה בַת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְכֹהֵן,
chunks.en: And about a young Jewish girl who married a Kohen,
that she may eat terumah,
and if she died,
her husband inherits from her.
And about a stolen beam that he built into a big building,
that he pays its worth.

chunks.he: וְעַל הַחַטָּאת הַגְּזוּלָה שֶׁלֹּא נוֹדְעָה לָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: And about a stolen chatas animal that the public did not know about,

words.note: A korban brought for a sin done by mistake.

chunks.en: that it gives kaparah,
to keep the mizbe'ach in good order.

mishnayos.summary: Testimonies about the blood of a neveilah, and about the parah adumah ashes or holy things that were partly touched by someone tamei.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beseira testified
about the blood of neveilos, that it is tahor.

chunks.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן בְּתֵירָא עַל
chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Beseira testified about
chatas ashes that a tamei person touched part of,

words.note: The ashes of the parah adumah.

chunks.en: that he made all of it tamei.
Rabbi Akiva added:
about the fine flour, the ketores and the levonah

words.note: The spices burned in the Beis HaMikdash.
A sweet-smelling spice put on a korban mincha.

chunks.en: and the coals, that a tevul yom touched part of,
that he made all of them unfit.

mishnayos.summary: A young Jewish girl married to a Kohen may eat terumah from her chuppah. And the Sages say that if we believe the witnesses about a girl taken as a hostage, we must believe all they say.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava testified,
and Rabbi Yehudah HaKohen, about a young
Jewish girl who married a Kohen,

chunks.he: שֶׁהִיא אוֹכֶלֶת בַּתְּרוּמָה כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה לַחֻפָּה
chunks.en: that she may eat terumah once she goes under the chuppah,
even before the wedding is complete.

chunks.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַכֹּהֵן וְרַבִּי זְכַרְיָה
chunks.en: Rabbi Yose HaKohen and Rabbi Zecharyah testified,

chunks.he: בֶן הַקַּצָּב עַל תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁהֻרְהֲנָה בְאַשְׁקְלוֹן,
chunks.en: ben HaKatzav, about a girl who was held as a hostage in Ashkelon,

words.en: who was held as a hostage

chunks.en: and her family pushed her away,
chunks.explain: They said she may not marry a Kohen.

chunks.en: and her witnesses testify about her that she was not
hidden away alone and did not become forbidden.
The Sages said to them:
If you believe that she was held as a hostage,

words.en: that she was held as a hostage

chunks.en: believe that she was not hidden away and did not become forbidden.
And if you do not believe
that she was not hidden away and did not become forbidden,
do not believe that she was held as a hostage.

words.en: that she was held as a hostage

mishnayos.summary: A widow from a family whose yichus is not clear may marry a Kohen. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel accepts this but says a beis din may not be set up to decide such families.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Yehudah testified,
ben Beseira, about a widow from a mixed family,

words.note: A family where we are not sure all are fit to marry a Kohen.

chunks.en: that she may marry a Kohen,
that a mixed family is trusted to say tamei or tahor,
to push away and to bring close.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
We accept your testimony,
but what can we do,

chunks.he: שֶׁגָּזַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי שֶׁלֹּא
chunks.en: since Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai decreed not
to set up courts for this.
The Kohanim listen to you to push away,
but not to bring close.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer testified, in Aramaic, about three things that are tahor or tamei, and people called him "Yose who allows."

chunks.en: Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer testified,
a man from Tzereidah,
about the ayil kamtza locust,

words.note: A kind of locust that may be eaten.

chunks.en: that it is kosher. And about the liquids in the slaughter house,
that they are tahor.
And one who touches a dead body
becomes tamei. And they called him
"Yose who allows."

mishnayos.summary: One witness is enough to say that a woman's husband died. And bones found in a wood shed are picked up one by one, and everything stays tahor.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva testified in the name of Nechemyah,
a man from Beis Deli,

chunks.he: שֶׁמַּשִּׂיאִים הָאִשָּׁה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד.
chunks.en: that we let a woman marry again on the word of one witness.
Rabbi Yehoshua testified about
bones that were found in the wood shed,
the Sages said:
he picks them up bone by bone, and everything is tahor.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer tells how they built the second Beis HaMikdash, and Rabbi Yehoshua says the holiness of that place stays forever.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said:
I heard that when they were building the Heichal,

words.note: The main building of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: they made curtains for the Heichal and curtains for the courtyards,
but in the Heichal they built from outside,
and in the courtyard they built from inside.
Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.he: שָׁמַעְתִּי, שֶׁמַּקְרִיבִין אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בַּיִת,
chunks.en: I heard that we bring korbanos even when there is no Beis HaMikdash,
and we eat the holiest korbanos even
though there are no curtains,
and lighter korbanos and maaser sheni,
even though there is no wall,
because the first holiness made it holy for its time
and made it holy for the time to come.

mishnayos.summary: What will Eliyahu HaNavi do when he comes? Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Yehudah, Rabbi Shimon and the Sages each say. The Sages say he will come to make peace in the world.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.he: מְקֻבָּל אֲנִי מֵרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
chunks.en: I have a tradition from Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
who heard from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher,
a halachah given to Moshe at Sinai,
that Eliyahu does not come to say tamei or tahor,
to push away or bring close,
but to push away those brought close by force,
and to bring close those pushed away by force.
The family of Beis Tzerifah was across
the Yarden, and Ben Tziyon pushed it away by force,
and another family was there,
and Ben Tziyon brought it close by force.
Ones like these,
Eliyahu comes to say tamei or tahor,
to push away or bring close.
Rabbi Yehudah says:
to bring close, but not to push away.
Rabbi Shimon says:
to settle the arguments.
And the Sages say:
not to push away and not to bring close,
but to make peace in the world,
as it says (Malachi 3): "Here I am,
sending you Eliyahu the Navi,
etc. And he will turn back the heart of fathers to
sons, and the heart of sons to their fathers."
